newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: GOLF-SJOLAND SMASHES COURSE RECORD WITH 61.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-SJOLAND SMASHES COURSE RECORD WITH 61.

text.p: Sweden's Patrik Sjoland smashed the Karlstein course record by three strokes with a 61 to grab a share of the Czech Open second round lead on Friday.
Sjoland was only a stroke off the European Tour record for 18 holes and his 10 birdies was two off the birdie record.
He joined Ryder Cup team hope Ignacio Garrido and another Spaniard, Miguel Jimenez, on 11-under-par 131 to set the early pace, three strokes ahead of the field.
Sjoland also equalled the best score of the year as he picked up six birdies going out and four by the time he came to the eighth tee, his 17th hole.
Needing two more birdies for a record 59, the Swede then twiced missed chances to do so, a putt of 18 feet spinning out of the cup on the eighth before he passed the hole on the last from 15ft.
However, by going back to a putter he used some time ago, he complemented good iron play with only 25 putts.
"I started thinking about the record after I birdied the fourth, my 13th hole," said Sjoberg, who briefly led this year's Italian Open.
"But when I lipped out on the eighth I knew it wasn't to be."
Garrido continued his Valderrama bid with a 65, while Jimenez posted 64.
Both Spaniards have chances for a place in their fellow countryman Severiano Ballesteros's Europe team against the United States at Valderrama next month.
Garrido, only six weeks after his maiden success in the German Open, is on the brink of selection, lying in 10th and final automatic slot in the Cup points table.

"I'm definitely more confident since I won my first title," said Garrido."Before winning, my mind was keeping me behind because I used to wonder if I'd ever live with great players like Langer, Faldo and Rocca and now I feel I can beat them."
